diagnosis.interpretation: The output truly changes head size; the reported zoom/pulse is consistent with its rapid scale corrections, especially around the blink. Rotation/translation of a locally stabilized head against the preserved neck/shoulders can additionally make it feel detached. The latter perceptual contribution is plausible, not separately measured.
diagnosis.prior_QA_limit: Large motion reduction and preserved mouth/blink correlation do not establish natural-looking movement. Sampled stills did not rule out temporal pulsing; owner moving review rejected it.

recommended_next_candidate.source: Original Q, not S or an already-warped derivative.
recommended_next_candidate.method: Apply dx,dy=0.25*(reference-smoothed Q eye midpoint), cap X±3,Y±5. Preserve the actual source face as one rigid translation region. Use existing smooth trajectory; no eye-distance or eye-angle compensation.
recommended_next_candidate.masking: Use the proven foreground isolation and observed-background restoration. Keep source mouth/eyes/head proportions rigid; taper only in the neck transition and do not move hands/torso.

limits: This is modest cleanup, not a promise of micro-expression-only performance; it retains most source movement.
No2D translation can remove3D pitch or yaw. Original apparent size changes caused by source3D motion remain, but no new scale is introduced.
Even5px local head translation can affect neck attachment; assess in playback, not just tracker statistics.
No rendering, media edits, audio changes, provider calls or canonical gate changes performed.
